A calmer approach to computer security

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerKeep software updatedProtect your accountsPause before respondingBack up and test recoveryIf you suspect a compromiseFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

Start with supported software, automatic updates, unique passwords, multifactor authentication, and recoverable backups. These habits address common risks without adding a pile of security utilities.

Keep software updated

Enable automatic updates for your operating system, browser, and essential apps. Restart when an update needs it. Remove software you no longer use and replace versions that no longer receive security fixes.

Protect your accounts

Use a reputable password manager to create a different password for every account. Enable multifactor authentication where available; passkeys or security keys can provide phishing-resistant sign-in when supported. Keep recovery codes somewhere safe.

Pause before responding

Unexpected urgency, payment requests, and sign-in links deserve scrutiny. Open the service directly instead of following a suspicious link. Verify unusual requests through a separate, known communication channel.

Back up and test recovery

Keep a separate backup of important data. Make sure at least one copy is protected from accidental deletion or ransomware affecting your main device. Periodically restore a sample file to check that recovery works.

If you suspect a compromise

Use another trusted device to change affected account passwords and review account sessions. Contact your organization’s IT team for managed equipment. Avoid installing unfamiliar cleanup tools or paying someone who contacted you unexpectedly.

Settings and hardware vary by device. Follow documentation for your specific model and software version.

What a VPN does—and doesn’t do

A VPN creates an encrypted connection between your device and a VPN endpoint. It changes who handles part of your network traffic; it does not make you anonymous or protect you from every online threat.
